neighbours.label: the comma or full stop ending a concessive or limiting clause (something one can't change or is busy with) just before a contrasting 'but'
fire: We can't undo the damage from last year's flood, but we can rebuild the bridge.
I'm swamped right now with exams, but I'll answer your letter next week.
You can't choose the family you were born into, but you can choose your friends.
Nobody can stop the rain from falling, but we can carry umbrellas.
I don't have much money at the moment, but I'd love to help somehow.
We can't control the weather on the wedding day, but we can rent a tent.
She couldn't fix the old engine herself, but she knew a good mechanic.
It's too late to save the old oak, but we can plant new trees around it.
quiet: We cleaned up the damage from last year's flood, and we rebuilt the bridge.
I finished my exams last week, and I'll answer your letter tomorrow.
You meet many people at university, and some become lifelong friends.
The rain fell all afternoon, so we stayed inside and played cards.
I got paid on Friday, and I bought a new coat with the money.
We checked the forecast for the wedding day, and it looked sunny.
She fixed the old engine herself, then drove it to the coast.
We planted three new oaks in the park, and the children watered them.
